concept.title: Mummy's Secret Ingredient
concept.big_idea: A short family skit in her own kitchen: a suspicious son and father try to work out what changed in the roti. Mummy confesses to the camera, reads the pack's own usage line, and the skit ends on a joke, not a product verdict.
concept.objective: Attention-stage creative test with this creator. A hypothesis, not a prediction: organic results do not predict paid performance.
why_fit: Creative DNA: Across 20 posts: formats skit (85%), still or carousel (5%); content comedy skit (70%), lifestyle (30%); language english (65%), hindi (30%); settings indoor home (80%), outdoor (15%); children on camera 40%; product shown 15%; sponsored 0%.

Skit format (85% of posts): A short family skit is the creator's native format; test it as an attention-stage creative and pair it with a clear product step. Caution: Mixed signal in ads: skits earn more 3-second views but have directionally LOWER click→purchase and ROAS.

Storytelling / narrative (90% of posts): Narrative is how this creator already talks; brief a short story with a problem moment and the product in the routine. Caution: Rule is generous: any 'relatable' or 'routine' cue counts.

Humour (75% of posts): Light situational humour is natural for this creator; use it to earn attention, and keep the offer/product step unambiguous for conversion. Caution: Ads: humour raises 3-s hook rate but 'no humour' has HIGHER click→purchase (stable candidate). Humour in ads is rare (15 of 97).
Attention alignment score 65/100 (AI-labelled posts vs paid-ad hook-rate patterns; organic engagement is not treated as evidence of paid performance).

tone.summary: Playful, expressive and relatable: comic exaggeration for the skit, a sincere plain-spoken beat for the product reveal.
delivery: Pace: fast in the skit, slower and clear on the product lines.
Language: English + Hindi mix, as in her posts.
Rapid character switching and text-overlay premise on the first frame.
The product is the 'secret' of a small domestic annoyance, never a lecture.
tone.creator_voice_in_profile: Her tone is conversational, expressive, and warm, often shifting between comedic exaggeration for skits and a softer, more sincere register for sentimental reflections.
tone.catchphrases_in_profile: Text overlays framing the premise; Rapid character switching; Expressive facial reactions; Domestic setting as a stage
tone.native_in_profile: A skit that presents a product as a solution to a minor, relatable domestic annoyance, such as a misunderstanding between family members or a household chore struggle.

avoid.item: Any claim that the product treats, prevents or cures anything, or improves immunity, growth, height, weight, brain development or strength.
avoid.reason: No such claim is verified in the supplied files; several older ads contain them (see restricted claims list).

avoid.item: Any number, percentage, multiplier or vitamin count that is not one of the verified product facts for the chosen product.
avoid.reason: Numeric claims must trace to a fact ID.

avoid.item: Superlatives and exclusivity ("best", "only", "No. 1", "bestseller", "loved by 10 lakh moms").
avoid.reason: Appear in older ad copy but cannot be substantiated from the files.

avoid.item: Comparisons with, or mentions of, other brands or products.
avoid.reason: Competitor kids-nutrition brands appear in several shortlisted creators' sponsored posts; keep the Little Joys video clean of them.

avoid.item: Third-party testing or certification claims (e.g. lab tested, Eurofins).
avoid.reason: Mentioned in ad copy, but certificates are not part of the supplied files.

avoid.item: Scripted taste or eating outcomes ("kids love it", "finishes it in two minutes"). Film real reactions only.
avoid.reason: Outcome claims are unverified; scripted reactions would misrepresent what happened.

avoid.item: "Doctor recommended", "expert approved" or any medical-authority endorsement the creator has not personally confirmed.
avoid.reason: Endorsement must be genuine and disclosed.

avoid.item: Age suitability, serving size or dosage statements unless supplied by Little Joys.
avoid.reason: Not available in the supplied files; left as [[CONFIRM: ...]] placeholders.
Every script ends with a disclosure line; confirm the platform's disclosure label.

avoid.item: Studio lighting, corporate jargon or a placement that ignores the domestic setting (her profile flags these as foreign).
avoid.reason: Creator-specific (from her/his own profile and posts).

avoid.item: Any joke that implies the food is hidden from the family unsafely or that the child 'must' eat it; keep the gag light and obviously staged.
avoid.reason: Creator-specific (from her/his own profile and posts).

avoid.item: Scripted claims about taste beyond the pack's own line; her sponsored track record is empty, so confirm disclosure habits.

scenes.voice: BETA: Mummy, roti ka rang thoda alag lag raha hai. MUMMY: Rang? Woh toh naya aata hai. BETA: Jaasoos ki nazar se kuch nahi chhupta!

scenes.caption: Mummy, roti ka rang thoda alag lag raha hai. Rang? Woh toh naya aata hai. Jaasoos ki nazar se kuch nahi chhupta!

scenes.voice: MUMMY: Ruko, bata deti hoon. Yeh Little Joys Proteinmix hai. Pack ke hisaab se: "Can be mixed into regular meals like roti, dosa, chilla, and pancakes". Aur "No taste change, no smell".
scenes.visual: Mummy breaks the fourth wall and holds the Little Joys Proteinmix pack beside the dough; label legible for 2 seconds.
scenes.caption: Ruko, bata deti hoon. Yeh Little Joys Proteinmix hai. Pack ke hisaab se: "Can be mixed into regular meals like roti, dosa, chilla, and pancakes". Aur "No taste change, no smell".
